facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 水_伤官 (Water carrying The Virtuoso). Persona The Virtuoso (伤官). Definition line: "Cross-current output, brilliance made of what it meets". Keyword Brilliance, charge fierce, poles catalyst Spark / friction Pushback. Family function: Expression. Cost dimension: brilliance against the grain; shining reads as defiance. Arena: the stage, spark, off-script, the note held too long. Classical portrait: brilliance and defiance; output that exceeds its container; 傲物气高, cannot hold its tongue. Ruled domains: Talent, Performance, Defiance. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 食神.
Element arena: Water (depth, current, tide, rain, spring, flow). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Metal generating Water cross-polarity — precision producing depth that exceeds its container".
- k2_overview: "Your Water moves as the Virtuoso: a current too clever for its banks. You express in floods of insight, subversive, fluid, impossible to police, the writer between the lines, the wit that erodes pomposity by morning. Nothing contains you long. The art is choosing what your torrent carves next."
- k2_functional: "Your expression flows subversive and quotable, satire and insight braided into one current."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Silver-tongued","Inspired","Free-flowing"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Talent":"Your talent is fluid genius: writing, strategy, humor, any craft where thought must flow around form. It resists containers and needs them. Choose loose ones, essays, seasons, series, and pour.","Performance":"You perform by currents: the essay that spreads, the remark that travels. Your stage is wherever words flow. Publish more, polish less. Rivers are judged by movement, not by stillness.","Defiance":"Your defiance dissolves things: authority mocked into smallness, rules outlived rather than fought. It is elegant and it accumulates enemies slowly. Now and then, defend something openly. It sweetens the water."}

- Sibling cell 水_食神 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Fluent","Nourishing","Easygoing"],"friction":["Drifting","Indulgent","Unmoved"]}
- Sibling cell 水_食神 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Following the day’s current instead of steering it is a habit now, whatever it started as. The Tuesday you set aside for writing became errands, a nap, and a show, and at no point did anyone decide that. The not-deciding is the whole mechanism."

Core element Metal, energy element Water. Law: Metal feeds Water (金生水: dew beads on the cold blade). Relative to the core the energy is the fed, so Water is this core's Expression. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Water on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Water as the Expression is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_水's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Whatever you are thinking is already being shared, and the editing happens after. You have more Water in you than time to settle it, so you share the thought ahead of deciding whether it is yours to share. It helps to remember that you choose what you share, even when it is true.

value_b.text: Holding a thought in is harder for you than sharing it, and out it goes. Being fully known matters to you ahead of being careful, so you share the story before you have told the person it is about. Remember that you get to keep a few things unshared until you have finished them.

value.text: Sharing it all is easier than choosing which part to share, so you rarely choose. Since you let out far more than ever comes back, you share every thought at full strength. You feel emptied afterwards because you shared the whole of it at once and kept none of it for yourself.

value.text: To stay honest with people, you share everything you think. Since you share openly rather than check what someone is ready for, you take away their choice of how much to hold. You are allowed to let people ask before you share it all, and the asking is theirs to do.

value.text: Mocking is your first language, and plain praise comes out like a foreign one. Since being clever feels safer than being seen caring, you mock what you love instead of praising it. Never forget that you mean the fondness more than the mocking lets on.

value_b.text: Mocking a thing is how you get close to it, and the ones you love get most of it. You mock rather than say what you feel, so your affection arrives as a dig. You hear the fondness under the mocking more clearly than anyone else can, and that part is yours to keep.

Since you sound mocking rather than moved, you hand them your praise in a form not worth keeping. Say the nice thing straight and leave it there, as the mocking is the only part they cannot keep.

value.text: Picking a fight with an unexplained rule starts before you have decided to. Since being told what to do feels like being made smaller, you pick the fight ahead of asking whether the rule had a point. It is worth remembering that you pick the fight more often than it picks you.

value_b.text: Fighting is what you do first with any instruction, before you have read it to the end. You care more about being free than being right, so you fight the very ones you agree with. You spend more on the fight than the rule was ever worth, and you already know it.

value.text: Any push gets a fight out of you, even a small one. You would rather lose on your terms than win on theirs, so you fight rules you never cared about and lose things you did. Skip the fights that do not matter, since each one you pick costs you a chance you wanted.

value.text: With whoever is in charge, you pick fights as your kind of honesty, audience included. Because you fight in public rather than in private, you cost the person above you their footing in front of the others. You could pick the same fight in private first and lose nothing by it.
